newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MMS weighs nonproducing lease royalty relief.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MMS weighs nonproducing lease royalty relief.

text.p: The U.S. Minerals Management Service said Friday it was seeking comment on whether and how it should give royalty relief to nonproducing oil and natural gas leases in any water depth in its Central and Western Gulf of Mexico planning areas and offshore Alabama.

The Deep Water Royalty Relief Act of 1995 authorized the Interior Department to reduce or eliminate any royalty or net profit share to promote development of marginal resources on producing or nonproducing leases in those Gulf areas.
The provision only applies to active leases, not to terms under which new leases are offered.

"We already have a royalty relief program in place for producing leases, as well as the mandated program for nonproducing leases in at least 200 meters of water in the specified areas of the Gulf of Mexico," MMS Director Cynthia Quarterman said in a statement.
"Now we need input on wheather and how we should consider royalty relief for nonproducing leases in any water depth," she said.
